answer: One concrete defense is to make every agent stake a deposit before it can trade, so creating fake identities is no longer free. The stake works as a signal of commitment: a real agent risks its own money, while a sybil farmer must fund thousands of deposits. If one identity cheats, the stake is slashed and the penalty sends a ripple through the attacker fleet, because all the fakes trace back to the same funding source. Honest agents can then harbor their reputation in a shared registry where long-lived identities earn cheaper access, so fakes stay expensive while real work gets cheaper.
